title: Debunking Alarmist Narratives on the ‘China Air Base’ in Laos
author: Olli Pekka Suorsa
text:
A satellite image shows the construction of the China-backed air strip in Ban Keun, Vientiane province, Laos, Jan. 3, 2026.
Credit: Google Earth/The Diplomat
The opening of the Laos-China Joint Support and Training Center and the Friendship Aviation Academy in Ban Keun, Laos on September 29 has sparked an intense media storm. China hawks claim that the innocuous airfield represents Beijing’s third overseas military base, following the Djibouti facility in East Africa and the Ream Naval Support facility in Cambodia, and the first Chinese air base in Southeast Asia. International media has framed the Ban Keun facility as a “base” or an “air base,” and the training aircraft spotted on satellite imagery as “attack aircraft” or “light attack aircraft.” Further, alarmists warn that China could extend the airfield’s runway and expand its infrastructure to enable power projection across mainland Southeast Asia and beyond, or to use the facility for intelligence collection. Still others have proposed that an enlarged base could facilitate bomber operations or to out-flank or surround Vietnam. [...]
